searchText: I figured out the problem. Thank you for support! Bug was that beneficiary gets touched (created) even if gas price is zero and we are not transfering any value. (This was related with state clear that I tried to debug with) One of tests that i would to see is authorization on fully empty account that gets its storage changed, all account in tests have at least some balanse. This tests how state clear with a eip7702 Yes! Great test! I think by EIP161 the account should still get cleared even if we write storage to it - right? (if it has no balance and zero nonce) That is what i want to figure out. And clearing would be my assumed behaviour here We have simulated this in an internal test in EthJS, the account should get cleared 🙂 Let me find the test Question is does that storage get saved or not? Nope, the storage gets wiped Would assume same The problem is that with EIP 7702 it is now possible (which was not possible before (except before Homestead I think)) to create accounts which are empty by EIP 161, but have storage EIP 161 defines accounts as "empty" if they have 0 balance, 0 nonce, and no code (but the storage does not matter) https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/blob/4c5d788cf9e25759bf3c650fb9a77b87fd4677a9/packages/vm/test/api/EIPs/eip-7702.spec.ts#L265 Here is the test 🙂 I have raised this concern on the EIP some times, but I think in the "new" version of the EIP this is not a problem anymore (or there was a proposed EIP which actually expands EIP 161 to also mark accounts with storage as non-empty) Ah, this one was proposed https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1080#issuecomment-2204191782 Ty for heads up, will check this Hmm I can't seem to find any proposed changes to 7702 which would mitigate this problem, and the EIP 161 deactivation also seems to be withdrawn. I was at the ACD call but I don't remember why it was withdrawn 😅 Nvm, found it <@429719902363058177> in the "new" version of 7702 (devnet-2), we have this line: `6. Increase the nonce of authority by one.` So, the account you write storage to will never have zero nonce 🙂 That solves it, good solution This is because a current issue with geth where the authorization does not work if the balance of the authorizing account is zero, but this will be changed to the default of zero: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/32f2ebf89075db51c54237c518ed99e784ceee03/tests/prague/eip7702_eoa_code_tx/test_eoa_code_txs.py#L38 fyi i just fixed this ^ but since we'll be changing 7702 a bit in devnet-2, i don't think we need to focus much on testing the current impl Yes good point 🙂 However, these kind of "bugs" might get triggered on devnet-1, and the case of the empty account now getting storage is not really an edge case I think PSA: don’t send 7702 txs in devnet 1 😇 > In case a delegation designator points to another designator, creating a potential chain or loop of designators, clients must retrieve only the first code and then stop following the designator chain. How would this work? Would it try to execute `0xEF0100` ? (in case of CALL) That's why we can never allocate `0xEF`, it's now a defacto "something is wrong" op code. Yes 🙂 But in the context of the change of 7702, I at this moment do not completely understand what *should* happen in case of multiple designators

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: I figured out the problem. Thank you for support! Bug was that beneficiary gets touched (created) even if gas price is zero and we are not transfering any value. (This was related with state clear that I tried to debug with)

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: One of tests that i would to see is authorization on fully empty account that gets its storage changed, all account in tests have at least some balanse. This tests how state clear with a eip7702

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Yes! Great test! I think by EIP161 the account should still get cleared even if we write storage to it - right?

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: (if it has no balance and zero nonce)

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: That is what i want to figure out. And clearing would be my assumed behaviour here

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: We have simulated this in an internal test in EthJS, the account should get cleared 🙂

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Let me find the test

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Question is does that storage get saved or not?

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Nope, the storage gets wiped

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Would assume same

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: The problem is that with EIP 7702 it is now possible (which was not possible before (except before Homestead I think)) to create accounts which are empty by EIP 161, but have storage

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: EIP 161 defines accounts as "empty" if they have 0 balance, 0 nonce, and no code (but the storage does not matter)

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/blob/4c5d788cf9e25759bf3c650fb9a77b87fd4677a9/packages/vm/test/api/EIPs/eip-7702.spec.ts#L265

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Here is the test 🙂

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I have raised this concern on the EIP some times, but I think in the "new" version of the EIP this is not a problem anymore (or there was a proposed EIP which actually expands EIP 161 to also mark accounts with storage as non-empty)

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Ah, this one was proposed https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1080#issuecomment-2204191782

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Ty for heads up, will check this

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Hmm I can't seem to find any proposed changes to 7702 which would mitigate this problem, and the EIP 161 deactivation also seems to be withdrawn. I was at the ACD call but I don't remember why it was withdrawn 😅

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Nvm, found it

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
<@429719902363058177> in the "new" version of 7702 (devnet-2), we have this line:

`6. Increase the nonce of authority by one.`

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: So, the account you write storage to will never have zero nonce 🙂

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: That solves it, good solution

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
This is because a current issue with geth where the authorization does not work if the balance of the authorizing account is zero, but this will be changed to the default of zero:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/32f2ebf89075db51c54237c518ed99e784ceee03/tests/prague/eip7702_eoa_code_tx/test_eoa_code_txs.py#L38

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: However, these kind of "bugs" might get triggered on devnet-1, and the case of the empty account now getting storage is not really an edge case I think

How would this work? Would it try to execute `0xEF0100` ?

excerpts.content: (in case of CALL)
